assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskite absorbers took photovoltaic efficiency from a few percent to over 25 percent in little over a decade, a rare case where a structurally simple ABX3 materials family changed an entire energy technology. Defect tolerance, tunable composition and solution processing give a clear structure-to-function story.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka made the first perovskite-sensitized cell, Park and Snaith (with collaborators) turned it into a solid-state, high-efficiency device. Kanatzidis, Gratzel and Seok also contributed decisively, so a three-person cut is contestable; I would favour the first cell plus the solid-state breakthroughs.
assessment.maturity: Independently reproduced worldwide and commercially pursued, so impact is established. Long-term stability and lead toxicity are unresolved, which could argue for waiting for deployment evidence.
uncertainties: Whether operational stability will be demonstrated at scale
Allocation among Miyasaka, Park, Snaith, Gratzel and Seok is disputed
Early efficiency records had irreproducibility and hysteresis artefacts

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nitrogenase underpins biological nitrogen fixation. Crystallographic determination of the FeMo-cofactor, including the interstitial carbide and the sulfur-displacement and turnover states, is the structural basis for understanding how a Fe-S cluster activates N2. This is structure explaining function at atomic level.
assessment.attribution: Rees and Einsle delivered the decisive crystal structures of the cofactor and its variants; Seefeldt and Dean (not in my three) contributed the mechanistic framework. Ribbe contributed cofactor biosynthesis and substituent chemistry. Allocation of the mechanism strand is unsettled.
assessment.maturity: Structures are well resolved and independently confirmed by multiple groups, with cryo-EM turnover structures adding support. The catalytic mechanism (E4 Janus state, hydride chemistry) remains partly unsettled, so recognition would rest mostly on structure.
uncertainties: Substrate-binding site and mechanism of N2 reduction still debated
Whether the prize should reward structure alone or include mechanism
Credit split among several strong groups

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation by PROTACs and molecular glues created a new therapeutic modality and revealed that thalidomide-class drugs act by reprogramming cereblon. The concept is original, chemically driven and has reached clinical trials.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies conceived and developed heterobifunctional degraders; Handa identified cereblon as the thalidomide target, a distinct but linked strand. Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto and Ito are also strong contributors. Allocation is hard but a three-person configuration is defensible.
assessment.maturity: Clinical translation is ongoing with multiple degraders in late-stage trials; approvals are still pending, so timing may be slightly early but momentum is high.
uncertainties: No approved PROTAC drug yet
Molecular glue and PROTAC strands may need different recognition
Many deserving contributors outside the proposed three

assessment.nobel_worthiness: MXenes are a large family of 2D transition-metal carbides and nitrides obtained by selective etching of MAX phases. Tunable composition and surface terminations yield conductivity, hydrophilicity and applications in energy storage, EMI shielding and catalysis. Close to my own area of inorganic and structural materials chemistry.
assessment.attribution: Naguib, Gogotsi and Barsoum (with Drexel colleagues) are the clear originators of Ti3C2 MXene and the family; the trio is a natural and fairly clean attribution.
assessment.maturity: Widely reproduced across many groups, with a rapidly growing literature; however, practical applications are still emerging and structure of terminations is difficult to characterise, so maturity is moderate.
uncertainties: Surface termination and structure are hard to determine precisely
Practical deployment is not yet established
Competition with other 2D material discoveries for the prize

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editing achieves programmable single-nucleotide conversions without double-strand breaks, a chemistry-driven protein engineering advance that extends genome editing following CRISPR. It is already in clinical trials and has strong chemical-biology character.
assessment.attribution: Liu is clearly the intellectual driver, with Komor and Gaudelli as lead trainee inventors; a single laureate is a fair configuration. Kondo and Nishida had a related cytidine-deaminase approach.
assessment.maturity: Rapid clinical translation and numerous independent validations, but the field is young and CRISPR was recognised in 2020; timing could be early.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2020 CRISPR recognition
Prime editing may be merged into the same recognition
Long-term clinical safety data are limited

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Surfactant-templated ordered mesoporous silicas (M41S, SBA-15, KIT-6) opened a new pore-size regime beyond zeolites and enabled templating of nanostructured materials. Their structures were solved with electron crystallography, a field I know well. Impact is substantial in catalysis, adsorption and nanocasting.
assessment.attribution: Kresge and Beck at Mobil made M41S, Stucky and Zhao developed SBA-15, and Ryoo pioneered mesoporous carbons and nanocasting. Credit is spread, and Japanese work (Inagaki, FSM-16) predates the Mobil report in part.
assessment.maturity: Three decades of confirmation; however, industrial uptake is limited, and a materials prize on porous solids was just given in 2025 for MOFs, which may reduce near-term chances.
uncertainties: Priority dispute with Inagaki FSM-16
Limited commercial breakthrough compared to zeolites
Recent 2025 recognition of porous frameworks

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Visible-light photoredox catalysis converted organic synthesis to single-electron pathways with mild conditions and is now widely used in pharmaceutical settings. Impact is broad, though conceptual novelty is partly in earlier inorganic photochemistry.
assessment.attribution: Yoon, Stephenson and MacMillan (a 2021 laureate) published the 2008 breakthroughs together; Nicewicz, Konig, Fukuzumi and Melchiorre also contributed. Because MacMillan is already a laureate, a trio of other contributors is a weaker configuration.
assessment.maturity: Widely validated and used in industry; the field is mature and timely, but credit complexity is high.
uncertainties: MacMillan prior Nobel complicates allocation
Priority relative to earlier Ru(bpy)3 photochemistry
Seven credited names, many deserving

assessment.nobel_worthiness: CO-functionalised noncontact AFM resolves the bond-level structure of individual molecules, a direct structural method that I value for its ability to show what was previously inferred. It has been used to identify reaction products and natural-product structures.
assessment.attribution: Gross and Meyer (IBM Zurich) demonstrated the CO-tip imaging, and Giessibl developed qPlus sensor technology that enabled it. Eigler and Ho are linked through earlier STM manipulation rather than this specific discovery.
assessment.maturity: Reproducible but largely limited to planar molecules on surfaces at low temperature, so general chemical impact is narrower than other candidates.
uncertainties: Limited to special surfaces and cryogenic conditions
Contribution of qPlus sensor versus CO tip is a separate strand
Impact on mainstream chemistry still modest
